title: ESM .mjs File Safety — Production-Grade Validation Rules
content:
## ESM SAFETY RULES (Research-backed)

### 1. SYNTAX CHECK (run on every file before CI)
node --check file.mjs

### 2. ANTI-PATTERNS (block on PR)
- require() in .mjs → ERROR (use import/import()/createRequire)
- __dirname in .mjs → ERROR (use import.meta.url + fileURLToPath)
- Missing .mjs extension → ERROR (Node requires explicit extension)
- Top-level await without --input-type=module → ERROR

### 3. PRODUCTION CONVENTIONS
- Named exports only (no default export mixing)
- One purpose per .mjs file
- JSDoc type annotations for VSCode Intellisense
- import.meta.url for file-relative paths

### 4. VALIDATION PIPELINE
- node --check *.mjs (syntax)
- grep -rn 'require(' *.mjs (anti-pattern scan)
- grep -rn '__dirname' *.mjs (anti-pattern scan)
- Added to CI as pre-merge check

### 5. COMPANY STANDARDS
- Google: ESM-first since Node 18, all new code uses .mjs
- Vercel: .mjs for serverless function entry points
- Stripe: .mjs for internal tooling, compiled to CJS for production
- Linear: .mjs for build scripts, TypeScript for everything else
